title: How Big Can You Get Naturally? (Nattyornot.com)
summary: NH tears apart the nattyornot.com article on natural size limits. He re-ranks the muscle growth factors with training first and genetics last, mocks the French 'PDC + 10' rule and the article's matching height-to-weight table, and argues these standards assume unhealthy 6-8% body fat. His conclusion is that naturals can get much bigger than such sites claim, citing old-school naturals and his own 210 lb at 6 ft.
claims: Nattyornot.com ranks growth factors with body chemistry, frame and muscle insertions on top and training eighth; NH says this order is wrong
Training should be ranked number one among growth factors because results are your responsibility
Body chemistry is a 'passive-active': lifestyle (diet, rest, environment) or drugs change it, so it falls under training and lifestyle
People who achieve nothing rank the factors they control as unimportant so they have an excuse
A wide frame with no muscle looks bad, while a narrow-framed lifter who builds muscle looks good; the active outweighs the passive
Obsession with genetics is a modern effect of drug users; bodybuilding discussion in the 1920s-30s focused on training
Most people who think they have bad genetics have average genetics
Lifting for years with no development means you are training poorly, e.g. wrong intensity or not enough volume, not that you're a non-responder
Chronic stress and cortisol damage muscle building and health; stress is an underrated part of recovery
Age is not a doom at 35; people like Jack LaLanne kept good physiques into their 40s, 50s and beyond by training
Cutting back volume and intensity in advance because of age or a cut causes the muscle loss people blame on age or the cut
Men are in their prime in their 30s and early 40s, not their 20s, if they keep training properly
NH's ranking: training, overall health, sleep, nutrition, stress, age, response to training, muscle fiber distribution, muscle insertions, frame, body chemistry
Most people who think they have low testosterone actually have a low-test lifestyle and environment
Starting TRT to bypass fixing your lifestyle has a price later
People underestimate their body fat: subtract about 5 points from anyone's claimed body fat percentage
People shocked at how much they must lose to see abs usually did aggressive bulks that added unnecessary fat
Bulking and cutting cycles were invented by pro bodybuilding; naturals of the 1920s-40s held roughly steady weight while gaining strength and muscle
Naturals should gain weight slowly and not fear some fat as long as muscle is being built
The French bro rule 'PDC + 10' claims your genetic-limit bodyweight in kg is roughly your height in cm minus 100; NH calls it bro science made by tiny people
NH is 183 cm and 95 kg (210 lb), well above PDC + 10, which disproves the rule
In France PDC + 10 is used like FFMI to accuse people of being on drugs or simply fat
Fat around and within the muscles makes naturals look bigger; losing 20 lb of it would just make NH look small
NH is about 16-17% body fat but most people would guess 12% because of his muscle-to-fat ratio
Nattyornot.com's table, e.g. 184 lb at 6 ft and 135 lb at 5'5", matches PDC + 10 exactly
A 6'2" man at 200 lb would look relatively skinny, so the table's 90 kg standard is far too low
The table ignores frame size even though the author ranked frame as the second factor
6-8% body fat is achievable for naturals but not reasonable; old-school naturals were around 12-18% and looked massive
Abs can look good at 10%, 15% or 17% body fat; too lean becomes detrimental for naturals
The author later cut 20 lb from his table, putting a 6 ft man at 160 lb, a standard that can promote eating disorders
Standards degrade if you hang around people with low standards or believe decline is inevitable
Telling people they must be very light and lean becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy: they starve, build nothing, and blame genetics
Trying to be 5% body fat as a natural is masochism and won't produce good aesthetics
Old-school strongmen like Sandow were around 90 kg at about 5'11" naturally; dismissing their photos as fake is dishonest
How big you can get naturally is unknown, but old-school and some modern naturals show the answer is 'pretty big'
A 6 ft natural with a narrow frame and average genetics can reach 210 lb with a full six-pack, so most people can get big
